title: Introduce trace-gatekeeper microburst smoothing to cut tracer overhead and improve tail fidelity
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Tracing hotpath cost has increased with growing QPS and high-cardinality requests. Existing sampling approaches either add too much allocation/CPU on the hot path or lose tail signal needed for incident RCA. Goal: introduce a lightweight "trace-gatekeeper" layer that makes a single, tiny hot-path decision (pass/hold/drop) using microburst-aware smoothing heuristics and a tiny in-memory sketch. Complement this with an asynchronous tail rehydration pipeline that reconstructs high-value traces for post-hoc analysis without increasing steady-state hotpath overhead. Success criteria: 1) Reduce per-request tracer allocations and CPU on hotpath by >= 30% for top-tier services. 2) Maintain or improve tail-event reconstruction recall for top-10 latency clusters (target >= 90% relative recall after rehydration). 3) No customer-visible latency regressions; error budget impact < 1% of baseline.
technical_approach: 1) Trace-gatekeeper inline shim: tiny fixed-size ring sketch + exponential decay window that tracks recent trace score and microburst rate. Decision is a single cache-friendly integer read/update; no heap allocations. 2) Microburst smoothing: use burst-aware thresholding to avoid over-sampling short spikes while preserving sustained slow requests. 3) Hold buffer: small per-shard in-memory fixed ring to hold minimal metadata references (no full span copies). 4) Async tail rehydration: held metadata is used by a background worker to request full spans from the long-form buffer/collector and rehydrate exemplars into S3/Historical store for later queries. 5) Telemetry: add new metrics for gate decisions (pass/hold/drop), hold-buffer occupancy, rehydration success/failure and latency, and estimated downstream recall. 6) Rollout: Canary on internal non-customer inference service, then staged rollout by QPS tier with kill-switch tied to occupancy SLOs.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Tradeoffs: the gatekeeper errs on conservative holds to preserve tail fidelity which may slightly increase background IO. Risks: poorly tuned decay/window parameters can either under-sample tails or overload rehydration workers. Mitigations: safe defaults from PoC, circuit-breaker on rehydration throughput, and goal-based autoscale for background workers. Privacy: held metadata must avoid PII; design stores opaque tokens only. Security review: not required for initial PoC (security_review_required: false) but will be flagged if holding changes to include request payloads.
rollout_plan: 1) PoC on canary service for 2 weeks (metrics collection): measure hotpath CPU, allocation, and gate decision distribution. 2) Tighten thresholds and add telemetry dashboards. 3) Week-long canary on internal customer-facing route. 4) Gradual rollout to low-impact external services (10% -> 50% -> 100%). 5) Post-rollout: keep rehydration monitor and automated throttles for 2 months. Rollback path: feature flag to disable gatekeeper per-service; emergency kill-switch in control plane.
metrics_to_monitor: tracer.allocs_per_request, tracer.cpu_nanos_per_request, gate.decision.{pass,hold,drop}.rate, gate.hold_buffer.occupancy, rehydration.requests_per_minute, rehydration.success_rate, tail.recall_estimate, infra.rehydration_queue_latency
comments: 2025-09-12 - Kickoff: scoped API surface and agreed on one-integer hotpath state machine. Attendees: Aisha, Marco, Nina, Omar.
2025-09-18 - PoC results: local PoC on dev cluster reduced allocations by 37% and CPU by 28% for the test route. Tail recall estimate at PoC was 85% before rehydration.
2025-09-23 - Design review: PM and Security feedback: ensure no PII stored in hold buffer; added opaque token mapping. Action: add schema validation and KMS encryption for rehydration payloads.
2025-09-29 - Implementation update: gatekeeper implemented in C++ shim and compiled into runtime. Initial benchmark shows +2us per-request hotpath cost vs baseline (acceptable).
2025-10-03 - Integration test: rehydration pipeline wired to historical store; rehydration success rate 96% on synthetic hold data. Preparing canary rollout window next week.
